messages:
maria (support): heads up — customer EX-7723 reports our API returning HTML when they requested structured json (response_format=json). client gets a parse error on their side. they say it started after our 03/10 deploy.

sam (eng-runtime): can you paste their exact curl + response body? also confirm if they're using strict mode / response_format param.

maria (support): minimal repro from customer:

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \n  -H 'Accept: application/json' \n  -H 'Content-Type: text/html' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-l-1","input":"{\"name\":\"test\"}","response_format":"json","strict":true}'

response (truncated):
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8

<html>
<body>
Error: unexpected token '<' at position 0
</body>
</html>

maria (support): customer says sometimes it's 500 with an HTML error page, sometimes 200 + html. they only started seeing this after deploy, and they have strict=true so it breaks their parser.

sam (eng-runtime): interesting — we should be ignoring request Content-Type for input payload (we parse body as json if body looks like JSON). but response Content-Type should honor response_format/negotiation. suspect a header normalization bug in the response path that treats some upstream error pages as html and doesn't set status code properly.

Kevin (platform): I dug into logs for that customer org id, saw a few backend handler exceptions around 2026-03-10 18:14 UTC. stack shows template-render fallback used inside error handler: it calls render_error_page() which sets Content-Type text/html and returns 200 in some codepath. that explains HTML body + 200.

sam (eng-runtime): ack. can you add the trace ids? we should correlate with request id and return to customer as interim. also we need a high-priority fix: error handler must not override status code for JSON-mode endpoints and must respect Accept/response_format.

Kevin (platform): trace ids: r:0a1b2c3d4e5f, r:0ff11ee22dd3. I created a quick patch to short-circuit template fallback when request has response_format=json or Accept includes application/json. test pass locally.

Liz (solutions): customer is on dedicated plan — they're impacted in production. can we give them a temporary mitigation? asking them to explicitly set Accept: application/json and Content-Type: application/json might help clients, but if handler returns template fallback we still see html.

sam (eng-runtime): mitigation: set header Accept: application/json and also include X-Force-JSON: true (we can accept that custom header for now) — I'll add a routing rule to check for X-Force-JSON and force JSON error responses for that org for the next 24 hours.

maria (support): passing to customer: please set Accept + Content-Type to application/json and we'll enable X-Force-JSON for your org. asking if they can reproduce with the smaller curl above.

response-bot: deployment pipeline:staging ran tests on patch 7c9f2 and all runtime unit tests passed. rolling candidate to canary.

sam (eng-runtime): plan: patch into canary (0.5% traffic) now, monitor logs for any html responses re: those trace ids. if green, promote to prod and postmortem. I'll also add a regression test asserting error handler respects Accept/response_format.

maria (support): customer confirmed repro with original curl and accepted mitigation. they provided one more sample body with schema drift (extra trailing comma) — will include in postmortem.

Kevin (platform): filed ticket PLAT-6219 for permanent fix and linked to deploy candidate. assigning to eng-runtime.

maria (support): thanks team — keeping customer updated. will follow up in #incidents if canary shows issues. :thumbsup:
